summary: Gone 10-foot pole L-4 tower on Stryker Peak in the Kootenai National Forest: built 1935, used until 1955, still standing in a 1978 photo; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Still standing in a 1978 photo; the Forest Fire Lookout Association Montana list marks the tower gone

events.note: The Forest Service built a fire lookout on the peak in 1935; FireLookout.com dates a 10-foot pole L-4 tower to 1935
CCC camp members had finished two of the five and a half miles of road up Stryker Ridge to the lookout, per a September 20, 1936 Missoulian item
Used until 1955; FireLookout.com says abandoned in 1955
Montana DNRC lookout point about 3 miles southeast of the summit, a converted school bus with cupola; the source says only 1960s, so the year is approximate
Stryker Ridge bus-and-cupola lookout (separate FireLookout.com record) listed as gone 1969; may be the same site as the 1960 DNRC point, not confirmed by any source
Photo showing the tower still standing

evidence.quote: This 10' pole L-4 tower, built in 1935, was abandoned in 1955.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FireLookout.com's Stryker Peak page says 24 miles northwest of Whitefish; its Stryker Ridge page, for the bus-and-cupola lookout, says 21 miles. These are two different records, so both are kept and neither is applied to the other.

sources.title: Stryker Peak
sources.publisher: Montana History Portal, Montana Historical Society

notes_for_editor: Stryker Ridge (FFLA list: Bus/cupola, Gone) is a separate record. Its listed coordinates sit roughly 3 miles southeast of the Stryker Peak record, which matches the 3-mile description, so it may be the same DNRC site; the editor should decide whether to merge or link them. The sources give no date for when the Stryker Peak tower came down. No source describes the site today.
